<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">NBT Bancorp Inc. is a registered financial holding company incorporated in the state of Delaware in 1986, with its principal headquarters located in Norwich, New York. <span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The principal assets of <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">NBT Bancorp
          Inc.</span> consist of all</span> of the outstanding shares of common stock of its subsidiaries, including: NBT Bank, National Association (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;), NBT Financial Services, Inc. (&#8220;NBT Financial&#8221;), NBT Holdings, Inc. (&#8220;NBT Holdings&#8221;), CNBF
      Capital Trust I, NBT Statutory Trust I, NBT Statutory Trust II, Alliance Financial Capital Trust I, Alliance Financial Capital Trust II and Evans Capital Trust I <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">(collectively, the &#8220;Trusts&#8221;)</span>. The principal sources of revenue for <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 13.3333px; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">NBT Bancorp Inc.</span> </span>are





































      the management fees and dividends it receives from the Bank, NBT Financial and NBT Holdings. Collectively, NBT Bancorp Inc. and its subsidiaries are referred to herein as (the &#8220;Company&#8221;). </div>

        includes upstate New York, northeastern Pennsylvania, southern New Hampshire, western Massachusetts, Vermont, southern Maine and central <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-align: justify; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; display: inline ! important; float: none;">and northwestern</span> Connecticut. The Company has been, and intends to remain, a community-oriented financial institution offering a variety of financial services. The Company&#8217;s business
        philosophy is to operate as a community bank with local decision-making, providing a broad array of banking and financial services to retail, commercial and municipal customers.</span><br/>

  <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold; text-align: left;"><ix:continuation id="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673202" continuedAt="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673203"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="Text_09fc9699604f49d8b35384da4ebcd002" contextRef="c20260101to20260331" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b31">
<div><span style="font-style: italic;"><span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Recently Adopted Accounting Standards</span> </span></div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673203" continuedAt="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673204"><ix:continuation id="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b31" continuedAt="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b32">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673204" continuedAt="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673205"><ix:continuation id="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b32" continuedAt="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b33">
<div style="text-align: justify; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: normal; font-style: normal;">In November 2025, the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) issued Accounting Standards Update
      (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) 2025-08, <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-style: italic;">Financial Instruments-Credit Losses (Topic 326): Purchased Loans</span>. The ASU expands the population of acquired financial assets subject to the
      gross-up approach in Topic 326, Financial Instrument-Credit Losses. In accordance with the amendments in this update, loans acquired without credit deterioration and deemed seasoned are purchased seasoned loans and accounted for using the gross-up
      approach at acquisition. The amendments apply prospectively and will be effective for fiscal periods beginning after December 15, 2026. The Company elected to early-adopt the ASU as of January 1, 2026.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <ix:continuation id="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673205" continuedAt="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673206"><ix:continuation id="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b33" continuedAt="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b34">
<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold; text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold; text-align: left;"> <br/>
    </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  <ix:continuation id="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673206" continuedAt="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673207"><ix:continuation id="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b34" continuedAt="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b35">
<div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold; text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold; text-align: left;">Accounting
      Standards Issued Not Yet Adopted</span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold; text-align: left;"><ix:continuation id="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673207" continuedAt="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673208"><ix:continuation id="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b35" continuedAt="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b36">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt;"> </span> <br/></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; word-spacing: 0px; white-space: normal; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify;">
      <ix:continuation id="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673208" continuedAt="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673209"><ix:continuation id="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b36" continuedAt="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b37">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In November 2024, the FASB issued ASU 2024-03, <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Income Statement-Reporting Comprehensive Income-Expense
          Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses</span>, that addresses longstanding investor requests for more information regarding expenses included in the expense captions presented on the face of the
        income statement. The ASU will require a tabular disclosure that disaggregates certain income statement expenses including employee compensation, depreciation and intangible asset amortization. In January 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-01, <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic;">Income Statement-Reporting Comprehensive Income-Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Subtopic 220-40): Clarifying the Effective Date,</span> which revises the effective date of ASU 2024-03. The ASU will
        become effective in the annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2026, and early adoption is permitted. Aside from complying with the new disclosure requirements, the adoption is not expected to have a material impact on the
        consolidated financial statements.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc316673209" continuedAt="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc3166732010"><ix:continuation id="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b37" continuedAt="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b38">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_88061d08b31547f99ff3b4cc3166732010"><ix:continuation id="Text_f9ddf5b138154269988cd86b5e7f08b38">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> In December 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-11, <span style="font-style: italic;">Interim Reporting (Topic 270): Narrow-Scope Improvements</span>, which clarifies the
        guidance in Topic 270 to improve the consistency of interim financial reporting. The ASU provides a comprehensive list of required interim disclosures and introduces a disclosure principle requiring entities to disclose events since the end of the
        last annual reporting period that have a material impact on the entity. ASU 2025-11 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 15, 2027, including interim periods within those fiscal years, with early adoption permitted. Aside from
        complying with the new disclosure requirements, the adoption is not expected to have a material impact on the consolidated financial statements.<br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    </div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Maturities of mortgage-backed, collateralized mortgage obligations and asset-backed securities are stated based on their estimated average lives. Actual maturities may
      differ from estimated average lives or contractual maturities because, in certain cases, borrowers have the right to call or prepay obligations, with or without call or prepayment penalties.</div>

<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify;"><span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">The allowance for credit losses calculation incorporated a 6-quarter forecast period to account for forecast economic conditions
      under each scenario utilized in the measurement. For periods beyond the 6-quarter forecast, the model reverts to long-term economic conditions over a 4-quarter reversion period on a straight-line basis. The Company considers a baseline, upside and
      downside economic forecast in measuring the allowance. From the second quarter of 2025 through the fourth quarter of 2025, the Company included an additional downside scenario with stagflation conditions, which is characterized as an economic
      environment where inflation rises alongside unemployment. Stagflation was identified as an emerging risk as tariff policies impacted the economy.</span></div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb4649" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46410"><ix:continuation id="Text_042efd0dc6874f5186bedd2a7c14e7355" continuedAt="Text_042efd0dc6874f5186bedd2a7c14e7356">
<div style="display:none;"><br/></div>
<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify;"><span style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-weight: normal; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> The quantitative model as of March 31, 2026 incorporated a baseline economic outlook along with alternative upside and
        downside scenarios sourced from a reputable third-party to accommodate other potential economic conditions in the model. At March 31, 2026, the weightings were 60%, 5% and 35% for the baseline, upside and downside economic forecast scenarios,
        respectively. The baseline outlook reflected an economic environment where the northeast unemployment rate decreases from 4.6% in the second quarter of 2026 to 4.56% by the end of the forecast period, with a peak northeast unemployment rate of 4.6%
        in the third quarter of 2026. National Gross Domestic Product (&#8220;GDP&#8221;) annualized growth (on a quarterly basis) is expected to start the second quarter of 2026 at approximately 2.75% and decrease to 1.72% by the end of the forecast period. Key
        assumptions in the baseline economic outlook included the Federal Reserve cutting rates with two 25 basis point cuts at the June and September meetings and the economy remaining at full employment. The alternative upside scenario assumes improved
        economic conditions from the baseline outlook. Under this scenario, northeast unemployment falls from 4.6% in the first quarter of 2026 to 3.7% in the second quarter of 2027 and eventually settles at 3.8% by the end of the forecast period. The
        alternative downside scenario with recessionary conditions assumes deteriorated economic conditions from the baseline outlook. Under this scenario, northeast unemployment rises from 4.6% in the first quarter of 2026 to a peak of 7.8% in the second
        quarter of 2027. The alternative downside stagflation scenario was removed in the first quarter of 2026 following a recalibration of the scenario&#8217;s narrative and model by the reputable third-party, which no longer provided a relevant stagflation
        scenario. These scenarios and their respective weightings are evaluated at each measurement date and reflect management&#8217;s expectations as of March 31, 2026. Additional qualitative adjustments were made for factors not incorporated in the forecasts
        or the model, such as loss rate expectations for certain loan pools and recent trends in asset value indices. Additional monitoring for industry concentrations, loan growth and policy exceptions was also conducted.</span></div>

<div style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: normal; text-indent: 0px; text-transform: none; white-space: normal; word-spacing: 0px; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); text-decoration-style: initial; text-decoration-color: initial; text-align: justify;">The quantitative model as of December 31, 2025 incorporated a baseline economic
      outlook along with alternative upside scenario and two equally weighted downside scenarios, recessionary conditions and stagflation, sourced from a reputable third-party to accommodate other potential economic conditions in the model. At December 31,
      2025, the weightings were 65%, 5% and 30% for the baseline, upside and downside economic forecast scenarios, respectively. The baseline outlook reflected an economic environment where the northeast unemployment rate increases from 4.5% in the first
      quarter of 2026 to 4.8% by the end of the forecast period, with a peak northeast unemployment rate of 4.9% in the fourth quarter of 2026. National GDP annualized growth (on a quarterly basis) is expected to start the first quarter of 2026 at
      approximately 2.55% and decrease to 1.8% by the end of the forecast period. Key assumptions in the baseline economic outlook included the Federal Reserve cutting rates with one 25 basis point cut at the December meeting and the economy remaining at
      full employment. The alternative upside scenario assumes improved economic conditions from the baseline outlook. Under this scenario, northeast unemployment falls from 4.4% in the fourth quarter of 2025 to 4.0% in the second quarter of 2026 and
      eventually settles at 4.1% by the end of the forecast period. The alternative downside scenario with recessionary conditions assumes deteriorated economic conditions from the baseline outlook. Under this scenario, northeast unemployment rises from
      4.4% in the fourth quarter of 2025 to a peak of 7.8% in the first quarter of 2027. The alternative downside stagflation scenario assumes deteriorated economic conditions from the baseline outlook. Under this scenario, northeast unemployment rises
      from 4.4% in the fourth quarter of 2025 to 6% by the end of the forecast period in the second quarter of 2027, with a peak northeast unemployment rate of 8.2% in the first quarter of 2028. These scenarios and their respective weightings are evaluated
      at each measurement date and reflect management&#8217;s expectations as of December 31, 2025. Additional qualitative adjustments were made for factors not incorporated in the forecasts or the model, such as loss rate expectations for certain loan pools,
      reversion adjustments for the stagflation scenario and recent trends in asset value indices. Additional monitoring for industry concentrations, loan growth and policy exceptions was also conducted.</div>

These relationships were in nonaccrual status and with <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossesIndividuallyEvaluatedForImpairment1" id="Fact_6e1d0c45bc984778995fcc4ff6f86854" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U002" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen"><ix:nonFraction name="nbtb:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossesIndividuallyEvaluatedForImpairmentNonaccrualStatus" id="Fact_f0000262686d41debb7a02bf59fc4998" contextRef="c20251231" unitRef="U002" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></span> allowance for credit loss as the fair value of the underlying

<div> <span style="font-weight: bold; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Credit Quality Indicators </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46450" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46451">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46451" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46452">
<div><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><br/>
      </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46452" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46453">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46453" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46454">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">The Company has developed an internal loan grading system to evaluate and quantify
      the Company&#8217;s loan portfolio with respect to quality and risk, focusing on, among other things, borrower&#8217;s financial strength, experience and depth of borrower&#8217;s management, primary and secondary sources of repayment, payment history, nature of the
      business and industry outlook. The internal grading system enables the Company to monitor the quality of the entire loan portfolio on a consistent basis and provide management with an early warning system, which facilitates recognition of and
      response to problem loans and potential problem loans.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46454" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46455">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46455" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46456">
<div><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><br/>
      </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46456" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46457">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46457" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46458">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Commercial Grading System</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46458" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46459">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46459" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46460">
<div><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><br/>
      </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46460" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46461">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46461" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46462">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">For Commercial &amp; Industrial (&#8220;C&amp;I&#8221;) and Commercial Real Estate (&#8220;CRE&#8221;)
      loans, the Company uses a grading system that relies on quantifiable and measurable characteristics when available. This includes comparison of financial strength to available industry averages, comparison of transaction factors (loan terms and
      conditions) to loan policy and comparison of credit history to stated repayment terms and industry averages. Some grading factors are necessarily more subjective such as economic and industry factors, regulatory environment and management. C&amp;I
      and CRE loans are graded Doubtful, Substandard, Special Mention and Pass.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46462" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46463">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46463" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46464">
<div><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><br/>
      </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46464" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46465">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> <span style="font-weight: normal;"><span style="font-style: italic;">Doubtful</span>
        - A Doubtful loan has a high probability of total or substantial loss, but because of specific pending events that may strengthen the asset, its classification as a loss is deferred. Doubtful borrowers are usually in default, lack adequate
        liquidity or capital and lack the resources necessary to remain an operating entity. Pending events can include mergers, acquisitions, liquidations, capital injections, the perfection of liens on additional collateral, the valuation of collateral
        and refinancing. Generally, pending events should be resolved within a relatively short period and the ratings will be adjusted based on the new information. Nonaccrual treatment is required for Doubtful assets because of the high probability of
        loss.<br/>
      </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46465" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46466">
<div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> <span style="font-weight: normal;"><br/>
      </span></div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46466" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46467">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> <span style="font-weight: normal;"><span style="font-weight: normal; font-style: italic;">Substandard</span> - Substandard loans have a high probability of payment default or they have other well-defined weaknesses. They require more intensive supervision by bank management. Substandard loans are generally characterized by
        current or expected unprofitable operations, inadequate debt service coverage, inadequate liquidity or marginal capitalization. Repayment may depend on collateral or other credit risk mitigants. For some Substandard loans, the likelihood of full
        collection of interest and principal may be in doubt and those loans should be placed on nonaccrual. Although Substandard assets in the aggregate will have a distinct potential for loss, an individual asset&#8217;s loss potential does not have to be
        distinct for the asset to be rated Substandard.<br/>
      </span></div>
</ix:continuation>

</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46468" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46469">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> <span style="font-weight: normal;"><span style="font-style: italic;">Special
          Mention</span> - Special Mention loans have potential weaknesses that may, if not checked or corrected, weaken the asset or inadequately protect the Company&#8217;s position at some future date. These loans pose elevated risk, but their weakness does
        not yet justify a Substandard classification. Borrowers may be experiencing adverse operating trends (i.e., declining revenues or margins) or may be struggling with an ill-proportioned balance sheet (i.e., increasing inventory without an increase
        in sales, high leverage and/or tight liquidity). Adverse economic or market conditions, such as interest rate increases or the entry of a new competitor, may also support a Special Mention rating. Although a Special Mention loan has a higher
        probability of default than a Pass asset, its default is not imminent.<br/>
      </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46469" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46470">
<div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> <span style="font-weight: normal;"><br/>
      </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46470" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46471">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><span style="font-weight: normal;"> <span style="font-style: italic;">Pass</span> -
        Loans graded as Pass encompass all loans not graded as Doubtful, Substandard or Special Mention. Pass loans are in compliance with loan covenants and payments are generally made as agreed. Pass loans range from superior quality to fair quality.
        Pass loans also include any portion of a government guaranteed loan.</span><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46471" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46472">
<div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> <br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46472" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46473">
<div style="text-align: left; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Consumer and Residential Grading System</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46473" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46474">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46474" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46475">
<div><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><br/>
      </span> </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46475" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46476">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46476" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46477">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;">Consumer and Residential loans are graded as either Nonperforming or Performing.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46477" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46478">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> <br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46478" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46479">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"><span style="font-style: italic;">Nonperforming</span> - Nonperforming loans are
      loans that are (1) over <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:ThresholdPeriodPastDueForLoansToBeConsideredNonperforming" id="Fact_2e393e98aa0d4f36b89bad142b35d621" contextRef="c20260101to20260331" format="ixt-sec:durday">90</ix:nonNumeric> days past due and interest is still accruing or (2) on nonaccrual status. </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46479" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46480">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> <br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46480" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46481">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> <span style="font-style: italic;">Performing</span> - All loans not meeting any of
      the above criteria are considered Performing.<br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46481" continuedAt="Text_391d0e4390d941cfbc3e7b87ddddb46482">
<div><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';"> <span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0); font-style: normal; font-variant: normal; text-transform: none;"> </span> </span></div>
</ix:continuation>

      </span> </div>

    <td style="width: 27pt; vertical-align: top; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">8.</td>

    <td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: left;">
            <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Defined Benefit Post-Retirement Plans</div>
          </td>

  </tr>


</table>
</ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_36ff15be62094e8bae4dbfc7b4134f741" continuedAt="Text_36ff15be62094e8bae4dbfc7b4134f742">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_36ff15be62094e8bae4dbfc7b4134f742" continuedAt="Text_36ff15be62094e8bae4dbfc7b4134f743"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:PostemploymentBenefitPlansPolicy" id="Text_3676a6dc63704593ac0ccf7c3411a701" contextRef="c20260101to20260331" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_af9eac3b83cc4baa94a337d5dff8d66f1">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has a qualified, noncontributory, defined benefit pension plan (the &#8220;Plan&#8221;) covering substantially all of its employees at March 31, 2026. Benefits paid from
      the Plan are based on age, years of service, compensation and social security benefits and are determined in accordance with defined formulas. The Company&#8217;s policy is to fund the Plan in accordance with Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974
      standards. Assets of the Plan are invested in publicly traded stocks, bonds and mutual funds. In addition to the Plan, the Company provides supplemental employee retirement plans to certain current and former executives. These supplemental employee
      retirement plans and the Plan are collectively referred to herein as &#8220;Pension Benefits.&#8221;</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_36ff15be62094e8bae4dbfc7b4134f743" continuedAt="Text_36ff15be62094e8bae4dbfc7b4134f744"><ix:continuation id="Text_af9eac3b83cc4baa94a337d5dff8d66f1" continuedAt="Text_af9eac3b83cc4baa94a337d5dff8d66f2">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_36ff15be62094e8bae4dbfc7b4134f744" continuedAt="Text_36ff15be62094e8bae4dbfc7b4134f745"><ix:continuation id="Text_af9eac3b83cc4baa94a337d5dff8d66f2" continuedAt="Text_af9eac3b83cc4baa94a337d5dff8d66f3">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">In addition, the Company provides certain health care benefits for retired employees. Benefits were accrued over the employees&#8217; active service period. Only employees
      that were employed by the Company on or before January 1, 2000 are eligible to receive post-retirement health care benefits. These post-retirement benefits are referred to herein as &#8220;Other Benefits.&#8221;</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_36ff15be62094e8bae4dbfc7b4134f745" continuedAt="Text_36ff15be62094e8bae4dbfc7b4134f746"><ix:continuation id="Text_af9eac3b83cc4baa94a337d5dff8d66f3" continuedAt="Text_af9eac3b83cc4baa94a337d5dff8d66f4">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_36ff15be62094e8bae4dbfc7b4134f746" continuedAt="Text_36ff15be62094e8bae4dbfc7b4134f747"><ix:continuation id="Text_af9eac3b83cc4baa94a337d5dff8d66f4">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Accounting standards require an employer to: (1) recognize the overfunded or underfunded status of defined benefit post-retirement plans, which is measured as the
      difference between plan assets at fair value and the benefit obligation, as an asset or liability in its balance sheet; (2) recognize changes in that funded status in the year in which the changes occur through comprehensive income; and (3) measure
      the defined benefit plan assets and obligations as of the date of its year-end balance sheet.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Basic earnings per share (&#8220;EPS&#8221;) excludes dilution and is computed by dividing income available to common stockholders by the weighted average number of common shares
      outstanding for the period. Diluted EPS reflects the potential dilution that could occur if securities or other contracts to issue common stock were exercised or converted into common stock or resulted in the issuance of common stock that then shared
      in the earnings of the entity (such as the Company&#8217;s dilutive restricted stock units).</div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>

            <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ReclassificationFromAccumulatedOtherComprehensiveIncomeCurrentPeriodNetOfTax" id="Fact_d269a516317646fbabc3677b4552e834" contextRef="c20250101to20250331_ReclassificationOutOfAccumulatedOtherComprehensiveIncomeAxis_ReclassificationOutOfAccumulatedOtherComprehensiveIncomeMember" unitRef="U002" decimals="-3" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">299</ix:nonFraction></div>
          </td>

    <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" id="Text_220f236c5c574055ae9540950688fbbb" contextRef="c20260101to20260331" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd1">

  <tr>

    <td style="width: 27pt; vertical-align: top; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">11.</td>

    <td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify;">
            <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</div>
          </td>

  </tr>


</table>
</ix:nonNumeric>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd1" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd2">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">
      <ix:continuation id="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd2" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd3">
<div style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">The Company is exposed to certain risks arising from both its business operations and economic conditions. The Company
        principally manages its exposures to a wide variety of business and operational risks through management of its core business activities. The Company manages economic risks, including interest rate risk, primarily by managing the amount, sources
        and duration of its assets and liabilities and through the use of derivative instruments. Specifically, the Company may enter into derivative financial instruments to manage exposures that arise from business activities that result in the receipt
        or payment of future known and uncertain cash amounts, the value of which is determined by interest rates. Generally, the Company may use derivative financial instruments to manage differences in the amount, timing and duration of the Company&#8217;s
        known or expected cash receipts and its known or expected cash payments. Currently, the Company has interest rate derivatives resulting from a service provided to certain qualifying customers and, therefore, are not used to manage interest rate
        risk in the Company&#8217;s assets or liabilities. The Company manages a matched book with respect to its derivative instruments in order to minimize its net risk exposure resulting from such transactions.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    </div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd3" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd4">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <div style="clear: both; margin-top: 10pt; margin-bottom: 10pt;" class="BRPFPageBreakArea">
      <div class="BRPFPageFooter" style="width: 100%;"></div>

    </div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd4" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd5">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">Derivatives Not Designated as Hedging Instruments</div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd5" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd6">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation>
    <div>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd6" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd7">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company enters into interest rate swaps to facilitate customer transactions and meet their financing needs. These swaps are considered derivatives, but are not
        designated as hedging relationships. These instruments have interest rate and credit risk associated with them. To mitigate the interest rate risk, the Company enters into offsetting interest rate swaps with counterparties. The counterparty swaps
        are also considered derivatives and are also not designated as hedging relationships. Interest rate swaps are recorded within other assets or other liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets at their estimated fair value. Changes to the fair
        value of assets and liabilities arising from these derivatives are included, net, in other operating income in the consolidated statements of incom<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';">e.</span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    </div>

    <div>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd7" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd8">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
    </div>

    <div>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd8" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd9">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company is subject to over-the-counter derivative clearing requirements, which require certain derivatives to be cleared through central clearing houses.
        Accordingly, the Company clears certain derivative transactions through the Chicago Mercantile Exchange Clearing House (&#8220;CME&#8221;). The CME requires the Company to post initial and variation margin payments to mitigate the risk of non-payment, the
        latter of which is received or paid daily based on the net asset or liability position of the contracts. A daily settlement occurs through the CME for changes in the fair value of centrally cleared derivatives. Not all of the derivatives are
        required to be cleared through the daily clearing agent. As a result, the total fair values of loan level derivative assets and liabilities recognized on the Company&#8217;s financial statements are not equal and offsetting.</div>
</ix:continuation>
    </div>

    <div>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd9" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd10">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
    </div>

    <ix:continuation id="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd10" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd11">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';">As </span>of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, the Company had <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:NumberOfInterestRateDerivativesHeld" id="Fact_68fa9106aa8a4d069e4469b6cd5d61f2" contextRef="c20260331_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_InterestRateSwapMember_HedgingDesignationAxis_NondesignatedMember" unitRef="U008" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">twenty-four</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:NumberOfInterestRateDerivativesHeld" id="Fact_e471c67e3dda44fdb3b949ca6c62a297" contextRef="c20251231_DerivativeInstrumentRiskAxis_InterestRateSwapMember_HedgingDesignationAxis_NondesignatedMember" unitRef="U008" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen">twenty-two</ix:nonFraction> risk
      participation agreements, respectively, with financial institution counterparties for interest rate swaps related to participated loans. Risk participation agreements provide credit protection to the financial institution that originated the swap
      transaction should the borrower fail to perform on its obligation. The Company enters into both risk participation agreements in which it purchases credit protection from other financial institutions and those in which it provides credit protection
      to other financial institutions<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';">.</span></div>
</ix:continuation>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd11" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd12">

    <ix:continuation id="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd16" continuedAt="Text_64934aa4b67841c8bb3f3cb11f5975fd17"><ix:continuation id="Text_f496b0a17b02451dad39fd96677d75f14" continuedAt="Text_f496b0a17b02451dad39fd96677d75f15">

      <table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" class="DSPFListTable" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; width: 100%; border-spacing: 0;">


  <tr style="vertical-align: top;">

    <td style="text-align: right; vertical-align: top; width: 18pt;">
              <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(1)</div>
            </td>

    <td style="text-align: left; vertical-align: top; width: auto;">
              <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><ix:footnote id="Foot_580b0fba5c6d4800960b79b2672fc895" footnoteRole="http://www.xbrl.org/2003/role/footnote" xml:lang="en-US">Netting adjustments
                represent the amounts recorded to convert derivative assets and liabilities from a gross basis to a net basis in accordance with the applicable accounting guidance on the settle to market rules for cleared derivatives. The CME legally
                characterizes the variation margin posted between counterparties as settlements of the outstanding derivative contracts instead of cash collateral.</ix:footnote></div>
            </td>

  </tr>

  <tr style="vertical-align: top;">

    <td style="text-align: right; vertical-align: top; width: 18pt;">
                    <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">(2)</span></div>
                  </td>

    <td style="text-align: left; vertical-align: top; width: auto;">
                    <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><ix:footnote id="Foot_8431d3732d7c479e8c759d27a115c43f" footnoteRole="http://www.xbrl.org/2003/role/footnote" xml:lang="en-US">Cash collateral
                      represents the amount that cannot be used to offset our derivative assets and liabilities from a gross basis to a net basis in accordance with the applicable accounting guidance. The other collateral consists of securities and is
                      exchanged under bilateral collateral and master netting agreements that allow us to offset the net derivative position with the related collateral. The application of the other collateral cannot reduce the net derivative position
                      below zero. Therefore, excess other collateral, if any, is not reflected above.</ix:footnote></div>

  <ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:FairValueDisclosuresTextBlock" id="Text_3f84c88d4c7b458c8dde4137c16fada1" contextRef="c20260101to20260331" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c1">
<table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; width: 100%; text-align: left; color: rgb(0, 0, 0); border-spacing: 0;" class="DSPFListTable">


  <tr>

    <td style="width: 27pt; vertical-align: top; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">12.</td>

    <td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify;">
          <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Fair Value Measurements and Fair Value of Financial Instruments</div>
        </td>

  </tr>


</table>
</ix:nonNumeric>
  <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c1" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c2">
<div><br/>
  </div>
</ix:continuation>
  <div>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c2" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c3"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:FairValueOfFinancialInstrumentsPolicy" id="Text_5ebf8c53e6514ad992503f4911dbd79f" contextRef="c20260101to20260331" escape="true" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f341">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">G<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';">AAP states that fair value is an exit price, representing the amount that would be received to sell an
        asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants. Fair value measurements are not adjusted for transaction costs. A fair value hierarchy exists within GAAP that prioritizes the inputs to valuation
        techniques used to measure fair value. The hierarchy gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities (Level 1 measurements) and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs (Level 3
        measurements). The three levels of the fair value hierarchy are described below:</span></div>
</ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <div>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c3" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c4"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f341" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f342">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <div>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c4" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c5"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f342" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f343">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Level 1 - Unadjusted quoted prices in active markets that are accessible at the measurement date for identical, unrestricted assets or liabilities;</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <div>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c5" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c6"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f343" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f344">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <div>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c6" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c7"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f344" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f345">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Level 2 - Quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices in markets that are not active or inputs that are observable, either directly
      or indirectly, for substantially the full term of the asset or liability; and<br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c7" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c8"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f345" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f346">
<div> <br/>
  </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  <div>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c8" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c9"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f346" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f347">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Level 3 - Prices or valuation techniques that require inputs that are both significant to the fair value measurement and unobservable (i.e., supported by little or no
      market activity).</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c9" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c10"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f347" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f348">
<div> <br/>
  </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  <div>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c10" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c11"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f348" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f349">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">A financial instrument&#8217;s level within the fair value hierarchy is based on the lowest level of input that is significant to the fair value measurement.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <div>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c11" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c12"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f349" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3410">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <div>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c12" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c13"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3410" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3411">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The types of instruments valued based on quoted market prices in active markets include most U.S. government and agency securities, many other sovereign government
      obligations, liquid mortgage products, active listed equities and most money market securities. Such instruments are generally classified within Level 1 or Level 2 of the fair value hierarchy. The Company does not adjust the quoted prices for such
      instruments.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <div>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c13" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c14"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3411" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3412">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <div>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c14" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c15"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3412" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3413">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The types of instruments valued based on quoted prices in markets that are not active, broker or dealer quotations or quotes from alternative pricing sources with
      reasonable levels of price transparency include most investment-grade and high-yield corporate bonds, less liquid mortgage products, less liquid agency securities, less liquid listed equities, state, municipal and provincial obligations and certain
      physical commodities. Such instruments are generally classified within Level 2 of the fair value hierarchy. Certain common equity securities are reported at fair value utilizing Level 1 inputs (exchange quoted prices). Other investment securities are
      reported at fair value utilizing Level 1 and Level 2 inputs. The prices for Level 2 instruments are obtained through an independent pricing service or dealer market participants with whom the Company has historically transacted both purchases and
      sales of investment securities. Prices obtained from these sources include prices derived from market quotations and matrix pricing. The fair value measurements consider observable data that may include dealer quotes, market spreads, cash flows, the
      U.S. Treasury yield curve, live trading levels, trade execution data, market consensus prepayment speeds, credit information and the bond&#8217;s terms and conditions, among other factors. Management reviews the methodologies used by its third-party
      providers in pricing the securities.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <div>
    <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c15" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c16"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3413" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3414">
<div><br/>
    </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  </div>

  <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c16" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c17"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3414" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3415">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';">Level 3 is for positions that are not traded in active markets or are subject to transfer restrictions.
      Valuations are adjusted to reflect illiquidity and/or non-transferability and such adjustments are generally based on available market evidence. In the absence of such evidence, management&#8217;s best estimate will be used. Management&#8217;s best estimate
      consists of both internal and external support on certain Level 3 investments. Subsequent to inception, management only changes Level 3 inputs and assumptions when corroborated by evidence such as transactions in similar instruments, completed or
      pending third-party transactions in the underlying investment or comparable entities, subsequent rounds of financing, recapitalizations and other transactions across the capital structure, offerings in the equity or debt markets and changes in
      financial ratios or cash flow</span>s.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c17" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c18"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3415" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3416">
<div><br/></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>

  <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c30" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c31"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3418" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3419">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Fair value estimates are made at a specific point in time, based on relevant market information and information about the financial instrument. These estimates do not
    reflect any premium or discount that could result from offering for sale at one time the Company&#8217;s entire holdings of a particular financial instrument. Because no market exists for a significant portion of the Company&#8217;s financial instruments, fair
    value estimates are based on judgments regarding future expected loss experience, current economic conditions, risk characteristics of various financial instruments and other factors. These estimates are subjective in nature and involve uncertainties
    and matters of significant judgment and therefore cannot be determined with precision. Changes in assumptions could significantly affect the estimates.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c31" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c32"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3419" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3420">
<div><br/>
  </div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c32" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c33"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3420" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3421">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Fair value estimates are based on existing on and off-balance sheet financial instruments without attempting to estimate the value of anticipated future business and the
    value of assets and liabilities that are not considered financial instruments. For example, the Company has a substantial wealth operation that contributes net fee income annually. The wealth management operation is not considered a financial
    instrument and its value has not been incorporated into the fair value estimates. Other significant assets and liabilities include the benefits resulting from the low-cost funding of deposit liabilities as compared to the cost of borrowing funds in the
    market and premises and equipment. In addition, the tax ramifications related to the realization of the unrealized gains and losses can have a significant effect on fair value estimates and have not been considered in the estimate of fair value.</div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c33" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c34"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3421" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3422">

  <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c35" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c36"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3423" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3424">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: normal;">HTM Securities - <span style="font-style: normal;">The fair value of the Company&#8217;s HTM securities is primarily measured using
      information from a third-party pricing service. The fair value measurements consider observable data that may include dealer quotes, market spreads, cash flows, the U.S. Treasury yield curve, live trading levels, trade execution data, market
      consensus prepayment speeds, credit information and the bond&#8217;s terms and conditions, among other factors.</span><br/>
    <span style="font-weight: normal;">&#160;</span><br/>
    <span style="font-weight: normal;"> </span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c36" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c37"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3424" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3425">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: normal;">Net Loans - <span style="font-style: normal;">Net loans include portfolio loans and loans held for sale. Loans were first
      segregated by type and then further segmented into fixed and variable rate and loan quality categories. Expected future cash flows were projected based on contractual cash flows, adjusted for estimated prepayments, and those expected future cash
      flows also includes credit risk, illiquidity risk and other market factors to calculate the exit price fair value in accordance with ASC 820.<span style="font-weight: normal;"> </span></span></div>
</ix:continuation></ix:continuation>
  <ix:continuation id="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c37" continuedAt="Text_070c65fbb03b4ab8a667ec272373170c38"><ix:continuation id="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3425" continuedAt="Text_a4f4c54cf0854cf1a7bdc6fa0df96f3426">

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: normal;">Time Deposits - <span style="font-style: normal;">The fair value of time deposits was estimated using a discounted cash flow
      approach that applies prevailing market interest rates for similar maturity instruments. The fair values of the Company&#8217;s time deposit liabilities do not take into consideration the value of the Company&#8217;s long-term relationships with depositors,
      which may have significant value.</span></div>

<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-style: italic; font-weight: normal;">Long-Term Debt - <span style="font-style: normal;">The fair value of long-term debt was estimated using a discounted cash flow
      approach that applies prevailing market interest rates for similar maturity instruments.</span><span style="font-weight: normal;"> </span></div>

    <td style="width: 27pt; vertical-align: top; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">13.</td>

    <td style="width: auto; vertical-align: top; text-align: justify;">
              <div style="font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt; font-weight: bold;">Commitments and Contingencies</div>

      <ix:continuation id="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b1" continuedAt="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b2">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b2" continuedAt="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b3">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company is a party to certain financial instruments with off-balance sheet risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of its customers.
        These financial instruments include commitments to extend credit, unused lines of credit, standby letters of credit and certain agricultural real estate loans sold to investors with recourse, with the sold portion having a government guarantee that
        is assignable back to the Company upon repurchase of the loan in the event of default. The Company&#8217;s exposure to credit loss in the event of nonperformance by the other party to the commitments to extend credit, unused lines of credit, standby
        letters of credit and loans sold with recourse is represented by the contractual amount of those instruments. The credit risk associated with commitments to extend credit and standby and commercial letters of credit is essentially the same as that
        involved with extending loans to customers and is subject to normal credit policies. Collateral may be obtained based on management&#8217;s assessment of the customer&#8217;s creditworthiness. Commitments to extend credit and unused lines of credit totaled $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:GuaranteeObligationsMaximumExposure" id="Fact_5cf88c49a0b944ce82e9344c558813bf" contextRef="c20260331_GuaranteeObligationsByNatureAxis_CommitmentToExtendCreditAndUnusedLinesOfCreditMember" unitRef="U002" decimals="-7" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">3.41</ix:nonFraction> billion and $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:GuaranteeObligationsMaximumExposure" id="Fact_48b275742820431990d751cf3004fba0" contextRef="c20251231_GuaranteeObligationsByNatureAxis_CommitmentToExtendCreditAndUnusedLinesOfCreditMember" unitRef="U002" decimals="-7" scale="9" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">3.40</ix:nonFraction> billion <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';">at </span>March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025, respectively.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b3" continuedAt="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b4">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b4" continuedAt="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b5">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">Since many loan commitments, standby letters of credit and guarantees and indemnification contracts expire without being funded in whole or in part, the contract
        amounts are not necessarily indicative of future cash flows. The Company does not issue any guarantees that would require liability-recognition or disclosure, other than its standby letters of credit.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b5" continuedAt="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b6">
<div><br/>
      </div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b6" continuedAt="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b7">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;">The Company guarantees the obligations or performance of customers by issuing standby letters of credit to third-parties. These standby letters of credit <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';">are generally</span> issued in support of third-party debt, such as corporate debt issuances, industrial revenue bonds and municipal securities. The risk involved in issuing standby letters
        of credit is essentially the same as the credit risk involved in extending loan facilities to customers and letters of credit are subject to the same credit origination, portfolio maintenance and management procedures in effect to monitor other
        credit and off-balance sheet products. Typically, these instruments have <ix:nonNumeric name="nbtb:GuarantorObligationsPeriod" id="Fact_c08a7d4e81c44c91815b5995a1589e60" contextRef="c20260101to20260331" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen">one year</ix:nonNumeric> expirations with an option to renew upon annual
        review; therefore, the total amounts do not necessarily represent future cash requirements. Standby letters of credit totaled $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:GuaranteeObligationsMaximumExposure" id="Fact_23b93152d9354c6bbe0ae74c5e66b12d" contextRef="c20260331_GuaranteeObligationsByNatureAxis_FinancialStandbyLetterOfCreditMember" unitRef="U002" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">63.6</ix:nonFraction>
        million <span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';">at March 31, 2026</span> and $<ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:GuaranteeObligationsMaximumExposure" id="Fact_336ce51a537d48c0accde74bbb107338" contextRef="c20251231_GuaranteeObligationsByNatureAxis_FinancialStandbyLetterOfCreditMember" unitRef="U002" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal">58.5</ix:nonFraction> million at December 31, 2025.
        A<span style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman';">s of March 31, 2026 and December 31, 2025</span>, the fair value of the Company&#8217;s standby letters of credit was not significant.</div>
</ix:continuation>
      <ix:continuation id="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b7" continuedAt="Text_5a52f25d59824e609f30a11de2e63b4b8">
<div style="text-align: justify; font-family: 'Times New Roman'; font-size: 10pt;"> <br/>

The Company accrues for material estimated losses from loss contingencies if the information available indicates that
          it is probable that a liability had been incurred at the date of the financial statements and the amount of loss can be reasonably estimated.</span><br/>

        <div style="text-align: justify;"><span style="color: #000000;"> </span><br/>
        </div>

        <div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000;">The purpose of this discussion and analysis is to provide a concise description of the consolidated financial condition and results of operations of NBT Bancorp Inc. (&#8220;NBT&#8221;) and its wholly-owned
          subsidiaries, including NBT Bank, National Association (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;), NBT Financial Services, Inc. (&#8220;NBT Financial&#8221;) and NBT Holdings, Inc. (&#8220;NBT Holdings&#8221;) (collectively referred to herein as the &#8220;Company&#8221;). When references to &#8220;NBT,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;our,&#8221;
          &#8220;us,&#8221; and &#8220;the Company&#8221; are made in this report, we mean NBT Bancorp Inc. and our consolidated subsidiaries, unless the context indicates that we refer only to the parent company, NBT Bancorp Inc. When we refer to the &#8220;Bank&#8221; in this report, we
          mean our only bank subsidiary, NBT Bank, National Association, and its subsidiaries. This discussion will focus on results of operations and financial condition, including capital resources and asset/liability management. Reference should be made
          to the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements and footnotes thereto included in this Form 10&#8209;Q as well as to the Company&#8217;s Annual Report on Form 10&#8209;K for the year ended December 31, 2025 for an understanding of the following discussion and
          analysis. Operating results for the three months ended March 31, 2026 are not necessarily indicative of the results of the full year ending December 31, 2026 or any future period.</div>

        <div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000; font-weight: bold;">Critical Accounting Estimates</div>

        <div><br/>
        </div>

        <div style="text-align: justify; color: #000000;">SEC guidance requires disclosure of &#8220;critical accounting estimates.&#8221; The SEC defines &#8220;critical accounting estimates&#8221; as those estimates made in accordance with GAAP that involve a significant level
          of estimation uncertainty and have had or are reasonably likely to have a material impact on the financial condition or results of operations of the registrant. The Company follows financial accounting and reporting policies that are in
          accordance with GAAP. The more significant of these policies are summarized in Note 1 to the consolidated financial statements presented in our 2025 Annual Report on Form 10-K. Management has reviewed the application of these estimates with the
          Audit Committee of NBT&#8217;s Board of Directors. The allowance for credit losses and unfunded commitments policies are deemed to meet the SEC&#8217;s definition of a critical accounting estimate.</div>
